name: Azarel
overview: Azarel is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Bani who had married a foreign wife. The Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this unique attribute. His mention is brief and focused on his family situation within the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Azarel means 'G-d has helped,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew elements for God (El) and help. This proper name conveys a sense of divine assistance or support, though the name was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Azarel is explicitly recorded as a descendant of Bani, linking him genealogically to this individual. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further family relationships for Azarel apart from his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Azarel's significance lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the post-exilic community in maintaining covenantal purity, as his marriage to a foreign wife was part of a broader concern addressed in Ezra 10. His inclusion highlights the community's struggle with intermarriage and the call to faithfulness to God's covenant during the restoration period.
